acceptance.given: An execution is evaluated using recorded source identity, command, exit status, and freshness metadata.

oracle.expected: Success is accepted only when all required identity and execution facts are present, current, unambiguous, and verifiable; otherwise terminal outcome is unsuccessful.
forbidden: Success is reported with unknown, missing, stale, ambiguous, or unverifiable identity or execution facts.
oracle.observable: Validator output and execution evidence show completeness and freshness checks rejecting any incomplete fact set.

acceptance.then: The success decision is emitted only after deterministic identity/execution validation.
acceptance.when: The operation is evaluated for success.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the success-decision validator with one required identity or execution fact omitted, stale, ambiguous, or unverifiable; it must reject success.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce a fail-closed success predicate that requires complete, current, unambiguous, verifiable identity and execution facts before success can be returned.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing verdict schema and fail-closed behavior; rollback only these predicate changes.

slice_hint.state_transition: evaluation with incomplete facts -> unsuccessful; evaluation with complete verified facts -> eligible for success.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Success iff every required identity and execution fact passes presence, freshness, uniqueness, and verification checks.

acceptance.given: Inspection resolves effective content and records a successful evidence artifact.

oracle.expected: The successful evidence artifact contains a binding to the exact effective inspected content identity (path and content digest) used by inspection.
forbidden: Evidence is unbound or bound to content different from the effective inspected content.
oracle.observable: Evidence validator compares recorded content identity/digest with the inspected effective-content digest and reports a match.

acceptance.then: Successful evidence is persisted with the effective inspected content binding.
acceptance.when: Evidence is recorded as successful after inspection.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Replay evidence validation against altered effective content or a mismatched digest; validator must reject the successful evidence.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Bind every successful evidence record to the exact effective inspected content identity and digest, with validation rejecting missing or mismatched bindings.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep evidence fields backward-compatible; rollback binding enforcement without deleting prior evidence.

slice_hint.state_transition: effective content inspected -> digest captured -> successful evidence bound to that digest.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Successful evidence is valid only when its content identity and digest equal the effective inspected content inspected in the same run.

acceptance.given: A bounded external process or aggregate executes with configured time or output limits.

oracle.expected: When a configured budget is exhausted, execution terminates deterministically with an unsuccessful outcome and records the exhaustion reason.
forbidden: A budget-exhausted execution is reported as successful.
Budget exhaustion lacks an unsuccessful terminal outcome.
oracle.observable: Process/aggregate execution result contains unsuccessful status, deterministic terminal state, and timeout/output-limit reason.

acceptance.then: The bounded execution reaches an unsuccessful terminal state tagged with budget exhaustion.
acceptance.when: The configured time or output budget is exhausted.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute a worker that exceeds its configured time or output budget and verify the harness observes deterministic unsuccessful termination with an exhaustion reason.

affected_subjects: Budgeted external process or aggregate execution
slice_hint.behavior_change: Apply bounded time/output controls to external process and aggregate execution and map exhaustion to deterministic unsuccessful terminal results.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Retain existing result schema; rollback only budget-to-terminal mapping while preserving process cleanup.

slice_hint.state_transition: running within budget -> budget exhausted -> deterministic unsuccessful terminal result.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: If elapsed time or emitted output reaches its configured limit, terminal status is unsuccessful and exhaustion cause is recorded.

acceptance.given: A verdict is produced from a candidate package evaluation.

oracle.expected: An independent validator reconstructs the current source identity and confirms real execution evidence supporting the verdict; assistant prose is neither required nor authoritative.
forbidden: Assistant prose is the sole or authoritative verdict basis.
A verdict is accepted without source identity or execution evidence.
oracle.observable: Validator report includes source digest/identity, executed command/result evidence, and passes when both independently match the verdict.

acceptance.then: The verdict is accepted only after source and execution evidence independently substantiate it.
acceptance.when: A verdict is evaluated or accepted.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Provide a verdict with assistant prose but omit or invalidate source identity or real execution evidence; validator must reject acceptance.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require verdict validation to derive from current source identity and independently captured real execution evidence, ignoring assistant prose as proof.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve verdict format and existing evidence records; rollback only independent-evidence enforcement.

slice_hint.state_transition: verdict proposed -> source identity verified and execution evidence verified -> verdict accepted or rejected.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Verdict acceptance requires matching current source identity plus real execution evidence; prose alone can never satisfy the predicate.
